1ow8bao:295: Agentic retrieval completely inverts the paradigm: retrieval is a behavior of the LLM, expressed through tool calls, not a system upstream of the model. In Claude Code, retrieval is exposed as a deliberately boring set of tools — Glob, Grep (ripgrep regex), Read, Bash (catch-all shell), and Explore read-only subagents. Each tool does one thing, and the control loop is plan → glob/grep → read → refine query → repeat (or spawn subagent) → compact → answer. The decisive difference: there is no pre-built index between the agent and the bytes — the retriever is whatever shell tool the agent chooses to call.
1r43z36:14: Tool Design, MCP, and Selection Decisions
1u125m4:268: The success or failure of agent-as-retriever hinges entirely on tool design. Anthropic's context engineering principle has only one core criterion: if a human engineer can't clearly state which tool should be used for a given scenario, don't expect the agent to do better. So tools must be self-contained, error-resistant, extremely clear in purpose, and each one should do exactly one thing. Model Context Protocol (MCP) turns this pattern from a Claude Code feature into an ecosystem default—every data source (filesystem, database, observability, ticketing, SaaS) becomes a unified set of tools and resources the agent can call; once retrieval is a tool call, every data source becomes a candidate retriever, no manual vector index construction required.
1v0zc9d:306: JIT loading also changes the shape of the context window. Traditional RAG spends tokens on chunks it guessed might be relevant; JIT loading spends tokens only on chunks the agent has judged relevant, skipping everything else. It not only withstands the criticism that "agentic loops burn more tokens" — combined with subagent context isolation it can actually save tokens: Claude Code's lazy tool loading cut context usage by roughly 95%. But JIT loading eventually fills the window too, so it needs a five-stage compression pipeline (Budget reduction → Snip → Microcompact → Context collapse → Auto-compact): load only what's needed, and gracefully forget what isn't.
